title: Linux printed “ready.” The shell still didn’t work.
deck: A CSR write latched a live interrupt bit and left the shell stuck. I fixed it and checked the result over UART.
excerpt: A live interrupt bit was latched during a CSR write. After the fix, the shell accepted a command over UART.
status: Interactive BusyBox ash and a separate program pass in full RTL simulation. Physical implementation is still open.

title: A smaller TLB made my Linux machine slower.
deck: An 8-entry TLB used 11.5% less mapped cell area than the 16-entry version, but the same run took about 32% more cycles.
excerpt: 11.5% less mapped cell area, about 32% more cycles to the same result.
status: Both 16- and 8-entry variants pass the shell/program gate. No routed SoC GDS from the physical campaign.

title: GPU inference on a PS4
deck: How I set up recoverable Linux on a PS4 and got Vulkan inference to return the expected output for short prompts.
excerpt: GPU offload passes the tested short prompt. Longer prefill still faults.
status: All 25 model layers offload with exact expected output in the tested short-prompt case. Longer prefill still faults.

title: Fixing secondary-CPU initialization in m1n1
deck: Why the timer-control register has to be restored after counter redirection and an ISB on Apple M3 and later.
excerpt: I moved one timer-control register write to the correct point in the setup sequence. The fix is merged upstream.

title: An RTL optimization that depended on fixed-point format
deck: A synthesis result looked useful in one configuration. A later format change exposed a problem with the assumption.
excerpt: The measured result held for one configuration. Changing the fixed-point format required a correction.
status: Working RTL optimization harness. Historical synthesis results are bounded to verified configurations.

title: Choosing better puzzles for Recast
deck: How I choose dice that support different ways to play and keep Daily puzzle data consistent.
excerpt: Current work on selecting letter dice, reviewing word sets, and scheduling Daily puzzles.
status: Solo game available on the App Store. The newer curation and scheduling work is subsequent development.

title: Tracing failures in dynamic agent teams
deck: How SOAR records delegation and tool use so I can tell where a run stopped.
excerpt: Clear worker traces make delegation and tool discovery failures easier to diagnose.
status: Research prototype with small exploratory evaluations. No claim of general benchmark superiority.
